entities.evidence: The days counted are those of Terah, Abram’s father, who settled in Haran in Genesis 11:31.
The death clause repeats the name of the man whose lifespan opens the verse.
The preposition בְּ marks חָרָן as the place where Terah died, the same place where his household settled in Genesis 11:31.

analysis.evidence: The phrase חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים וּמָאתַיִם שָׁנָה gives the total for יְמֵי תֶרַח. Terah’s days amounted to 205 years.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural, with prefixed conjunction וַ־. The verb agrees with יְמֵי, the masculine plural construct head of יְמֵי תֶרַח, “the days of Terah.”
analysis.sense: to be (of a quantity or duration), to amount to

analysis.evidence: The verse gives יְמֵי תֶרַח, “the days of Terah,” as 205 years and then records his death in Haran. The phrase denotes his lifetime.
analysis.morphology: יְמֵי is the masculine plural construct of the common noun יוֹם. Its complement is תֶרַח (Terah).
analysis.sense: (pl.) days of a life, a reign or an age

analysis.evidence: יְמֵי תֶרַח means “the days of Terah.” The verse names him again in וַיָּמָת תֶּרַח, “and Terah died,” confirming whose lifespan is being counted.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix. It follows the construct plural יְמֵי, “days of.”
analysis.sense: The personal name of the man whose lifespan is given.

analysis.evidence: After giving Terah’s lifespan as 205 years, the verse says וַיָּמָת תֶּרַח בְּחָרָן, “and Terah died in Haran.”
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, agreeing with תֶּרַח.
analysis.sense: die, come to the end of life

analysis.evidence: The opening phrase יְמֵי תֶרַח introduces Terah’s lifespan. The closing clause וַיָּמָת תֶּרַח בְּחָרָן, “and Terah died in Haran,” repeats his name to identify the man who died.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun without a prefix or suffix. It is the subject of וַיָּמָת, “and he died.”
analysis.sense: The personal name of the man whose lifespan is given.

analysis.evidence: In וַיָּמָת תֶּרַח בְּחָרָן, Terah is the subject of וַיָּמָת, “died,” and בְּחָרָן identifies where he died.
analysis.morphology: The locative preposition בְּ is prefixed to the place name חָרָן.
analysis.sense: Haran, the place where Terah settled and died.
